summary.text: 備 is interpreted as a person carrying an arrow container, a scene associated with being equipped and ready. The 1956 scheme adopted 备 as the simplified form corresponding to 備; modern glosses include “prepare” and “ready.”

formation.text: 備 is analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 人 depicts a person, while 𤰈 depicts arrows in a container and is also assigned a sound role. Together, the parts have been interpreted as a person carrying a quiver, a scene linked with preparedness. The sound analysis is supported by a proposed Zhengzhang Old Chinese comparison, but an independent historical reading for 𤰈 is unavailable here. 备 corresponds to 備 in the 1956 simplification scheme.

components.text: In 備, 人 depicts the person in the interpreted carrying scene associated with preparedness.
In 備, 𤰈 depicts arrows in a container, identified in texts as a quiver. It is also assigned a sound role, though its historical pronunciation is not independently verified here.

sound_limitation.text: A Zhengzhang Old Chinese comparison is reported, but no independent character-specific historical reading for 𤰈 was retrieved to verify its pronunciation or sound role.

sound.text: The proposed Zhengzhang Old Chinese forms *bɯɡ and *brɯɡs share initial and rhyme material; 備 has additional final *s. This comparison does not independently confirm 𤰈’s reading.

components.text: 备 is the officially adopted simplified form corresponding to 備. A secondary account proposes a route through variant 俻, but the official scheme does not establish that derivation.

history.text: 備 is recorded in oracle-bone, bronze, and manuscript script categories, but its earliest appearance is not dated here. No glyph images are included to illustrate those categories.

The right-hand component is printed as 𤰇 in some forms and described as a change from seal-script 𤰈. In bronze forms, its lower part is also reported to change to 用, tentatively interpreted as a sound element; a complete dated sequence is not established.
The 1956 simplification scheme lists 备 as corresponding to 備. 俻 was separately recognized as a variant of 備, but the scheme does not identify it as the direct source of 备.

uncertainties.text: The carrying-quiver interpretation links the graph with preparedness but does not establish the spoken word’s earliest meaning. Texts identify the pictured container as 箙, and 備 reportedly writes 箙 in a bronze inscription; neither establishes the pictured object’s original name or proves a sound match between that name and 𤰈.

備 has recorded glosses including prepared or complete, for use, cautious, equipment, and all or entirely. The cited examples do not establish a complete chronology or continuous development among these meanings.

senses.text: Bronze uses are reported with glosses such as “equipped” or “complete” and “for use.” The carrying-quiver scene may help explain preparedness, but does not prove the word’s earliest spoken sense.

senses.period: received lexicographic tradition; date of spoken sense unresolved
senses.text: The received dictionary gloss 慎也 means “cautious” or “careful”; it does not establish the earliest spoken meaning.
Dictionary citations include uses glossed “all” or “entirely,” but do not establish when this sense arose or how it relates chronologically to preparation or completeness.
Later cited examples use 備 for equipment or facilities. The evidence does not establish that this meaning followed a particular earlier sense.

limitations.text: The earliest attested spoken sense is unresolved. Reported bronze contexts and received dictionary glosses do not provide a complete dated history of the meanings.

A bronze inscription reportedly uses 備 as a whole-graph loan for 箙, “quiver”: the sign 備 was reused to write this different word because of a proposed sound resemblance, rather than because “prepare” developed into “quiver.” The resemblance is not independently demonstrated, and the pictured object’s original name is unresolved.
